sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: In unit 13 you added *-ok*, *-ek* or *-ök* to the stem to say “I”. To say “we”, add *-unk* or *-ünk* to the same stem. The ending says who acts, so *olvasunk* already means “we read”.

sections.title: Which ending?
sections.content: A stem with a back vowel (*a, á, o, ó, u, ú*) takes *-unk*: *olvas* becomes *olvasunk*, *tanul* becomes *tanulunk*. A stem with a front vowel (*e, é, ö, ő, ü, ű*) takes *-ünk*: *beszél* becomes *beszélünk*, *főz* becomes *főzünk*. There are only two endings here, not three: *e* and *ö* both take *-ünk*.

items.english: We wake up in the morning.

sections.content: *Ír* has only the neutral vowel *í*, so it follows the pattern of *írok*: learn it as it is, *írunk*.
